record.paper_title: Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II: Examples, Applications and Open Problems
record.original_question: For the finite simple groups SL_n(F_p) and related groups of Lie type, is there a uniform positive lower bound on the cocycle Cheeger constants in permutations for the Steinberg presentations, at least when n is fixed and p tends to infinity, while the cocycle Cheeger constants for the short Guralnick-Kantor-Kassabov-Lubotzky presentations tend to zero when either n or p tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.7. There is a uniform lower bound on the cocycle Cheeger constant in permutations of the Steinberg presentations, at least when fixing n and tending p to ∞. On the contrary, the cocycle Cheeger constants in permutations of the GKKL presentations tend to zero when either n or p tending to ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup.

Let G be a finite group and let P = ⟨S | R⟩ be a finite presentation of G, where S is a finite generating set and R ⊆ F(S) is a finite set of relators. For an integer n ≥ 1, let Sym(n) denote the symmetric group on n letters, endowed with the normalized Hamming metric d_H(σ, τ) = (1/n)·#{ i : σ(i) ≠ τ(i) }.

For a tuple φ : S → Sym(n) (an "almost-homomorphism"), its defect with respect to P is
  def_P(φ) := (1/|R|) · Σ_{r ∈ R} d_H( r(φ(s_1), …, φ(s_k)), id ),
and its distance to an honest homomorphism is
  dist(φ, Hom(G, Sym(n))) := min_{ψ ∈ Hom(G,Sym(n))} max_{s ∈ S} d_H(φ(s), ψ(s)).

The cocycle Cheeger constant in permutations of the presentation P is
  h(P) := lim inf_{n → ∞}  inf_{ φ : S → Sym(n), φ not a homomorphism }  def_P(φ) / dist(φ, Hom(G, Sym(n))).

(Equivalently, h(P) is the optimal linear rate of permutation cocycle stability of P; a positive value of h(P) means P is linearly stable in permutations.)

Two families of presentations for G = SL_n(F_p) (n ≥ 3 fixed, p prime).

(i) The Steinberg presentations: the standard presentation of SL_n(F_p) on the elementary root subgroup generators {e_{ij}(t) : 1 ≤ i ≠ j ≤ n, t ∈ F_p}, with the Steinberg/Chevalley commutator relations and additive/multiplicative relations among root elements.

(ii) The short Guralnick–Kantor–Kassabov–Lubotzky (GKKL) presentations: the bounded-length presentations of SL_n(F_p) constructed so that the number of generators and relators, and the total length of the relators, are bounded by a polylogarithmic (in fact poly(log(np))) function of n and p.

Problem. Establish the following two assertions:

(a) There exists a constant c > 0, independent of p, such that for every fixed n ≥ 3 the Steinberg presentation P_n^{St}(p) of SL_n(F_p) satisfies h(P_n^{St}(p)) ≥ c for all sufficiently large primes p. (More ambitiously, the bound is uniform in both n and p.)

(b) For the short GKKL presentations P_{n,p}^{GKKL} of SL_n(F_p), one has h(P_{n,p}^{GKKL}) → 0 as either n → ∞ (with p fixed) or p → ∞ (with n fixed).

Prove or disprove (a) and (b).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears as an open problem in the literature on stability of homomorphisms, coverings, and cocycles. Recent related work (e.g., 2025 preprints on cocycle stability in permutations of random simplicial complexes) treats the cocycle Cheeger constant framework but does not establish the claimed uniform lower bound for Steinberg presentations or the vanishing for short GKKL presentations of SL_n(F_p). No resolution was found.

status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 6.7. There is a uniform lower bound on the cocycle Cheeger constant in permutations of the Steinberg presentations, ... GKKL presentations tend to zero ...
status_evidence.claim: The statement is posed as an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Cocycle stability in permutations of random simplicial complexes
status_evidence.snippet: Lubotzky and collaborators initiated the study of the cocycle stability rate of complexes with permutation coefficients ... defined the appropriate Cheeger constant in this context.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work develops the framework but does not resolve the conjecture.
